page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance from the c2d server family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, utilizing a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 64 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and contains zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% with a stress-ng single-core score of 2928.59. Multi-core CPU performance falls within the average range, scoring 11730.12 on stress-ng and 6622.0 on Geekbench. Memory bandwidth benchmarks indicate average performance, with read-only small block cached speeds at 553.05 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds at 62.15 GB/sec. Large block write speeds reach 39.95 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression operations also align with average tiers, showing a PassMark CPU encryption score of 9278.94 and single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 28.36 GB/sec.

The high memory-to-vCPU ratio makes this instance suitable for memory-intensive workloads such as database operations, caching layers, and software compilation. PassMark database operations scored 3786.37, and Redis SET operations achieved 8.97 million operations per second, both placing in the average tier. However, the instance exhibits a performance bottleneck in large-scale language model processing; prompt processing for a medium 7B model is weak, registering at 18.65 tokens per second, and large 70B model inference is unsupported due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. The instance represents a balanced cost-efficiency profile for memory-heavy tasks that do not require local NVMe storage or high-density parallel compute.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 64 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core and a dedicated CPU allocation. The instance lacks bundled local storage and GPU accelerators. In performance testing, it delivers strong single-core CPU capabilities, scoring in the top 25% on stress-ng, while multi-core performance and memory bandwidth remain in the average tier. Database operations and Redis SET throughput also perform at average levels, making the instance suitable for memory-intensive applications, caching layers, and database workloads. However, it exhibits weak performance in medium-model LLM prompt processing and is not configured for large-scale AI inference. It offers a qualitative balance of high memory density per vCPU for workloads that do not require local NVMe storage.
